svg.title: Health Endpoint Monitoring
svg.desc: Health Endpoint Monitoring. Expose liveness and readiness checks that load balancers and monitors probe. Step 1, Three questions: While A boots, the startup check holds the other two off; traffic starts only once /readyz passes. Step 2, Not ready: no traffic: A loses its database connections: /readyz says 503, so it gets no traffic, and nothing restarts it. Step 3, Not alive: restart: The process deadlocks and /livez stops answering: after 3 failed probes the orchestrator restarts A. Step 4, Don't fail all at once: A shared database browns out: deep checks fail everywhere at once. Stay shallow, alert from outside.

g.text: While A boots, the startup check holds the other two off; traffic starts only once /readyz passes.
A loses its database connections: /readyz says 503, so it gets no traffic, and nothing restarts it.
The process deadlocks and /livez stops answering: after 3 failed probes the orchestrator restarts A.
A shared database browns out: deep checks fail everywhere at once. Stay shallow, alert from outside.
Can it serve requests right now?
if it also tests the database…
The monitor calls the public endpoint from outside, as a user would: it sees the whole path.
Illustrative thresholds: one /readyz answer moves A in or out, 3 missed /livez probes restart it.
Liveness never tests dependencies: restarting an instance does not repair a database.
Alternative: a balancer that fails open keeps routing when every target looks unhealthy.
